UnitStatement: DEL-03-01 is the AgentEnginePort and Engine Conformance Suite deliverable under package PKG-03 (Runtime Engine Contract and Turn Lifecycle).
DEL-03-01 uses DecompositionVariant SOFTWARE_DECOMP at revision v3.2.
DEL-03-01 is typed API_CONTRACT with ContextEnvelope M, covers scope item SOW-037, and supports objective OBJ-002.
Anticipated artifacts for DEL-03-01 are agent-engine-port.ts, runtime contract docs, and conformance tests.
Contract identity is AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract per docs/SPEC.md section 10.1 and docs/TYPES.md section 7.1.
Chirality owns the runtime contract; SDK APIs do not define public harness semantics.
EngineAdapter is the provider/SDK-specific implementation behind AgentEnginePort.
The primary operation is runTurn(input: TurnInput): AsyncIterable<UIEvent>.
The optional operation is interrupt?(sessionId: string): Promise<void>.
The browser stream contract is a UIEvent stream using stable SSE names.
The canonical runtime record is HarnessEvent records stored in product-owned event JSONL.
Required conformance subjects are the stub adapter and the SDK-backed adapter.
The SDK-backed adapter must pass engine conformance before default production use.
Public APIs, canonical event schemas, session storage contracts, permission decision records, and governance rules must not become SDK-shaped.
Existing /api/harness/* route shapes must remain stable during SDK adoption and TurnEngine extraction.
Browser-facing SSE event names must remain compatible during SDK adoption.
Accepted turns must persist terminal success, failure, cancellation, or interruption outcomes.
Accepted user input must be persisted before SDK/model execution begins.
SDK identifiers, message names, permission modes, tool names, transcript paths, and session IDs are treated as adapter metadata.
docs/PRD.md is accessible but _REFERENCES.md reports HASH_MISMATCH for REF-006; PRD-derived content should be reconfirmed before acceptance.
The runtime contract module is agent-engine-port.ts or an equivalent product-owned runtime contract.
The TypeScript interface AgentEnginePort exposes runTurn and optional interrupt.
TurnInput must include active session, normalized project root, persona, mode, resolved runtime options, content blocks, attachment summaries, and a cancellation signal where applicable.
The conformance suite is engine-conformance.ts or equivalent tests for stub and SDK-backed adapters.
A deterministic stub adapter is retained for tests.
The SDK-backed adapter is the provider implementation behind the product-owned contract.

DEL-03-01 exists to make the runtime engine replaceable by construction while allowing the Claude Agent SDK as the preferred implementation substrate when it satisfies Chirality-owned governance, audit, permission, session, and route-compatibility requirements.
The decomposition assigns DEL-03-01 to SOW-037 and OBJ-002: define the product-owned AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract and conformance tests before SDK behavior becomes production default.
Contract names, public APIs, browser events, persisted events, permission decisions, and session records should use Chirality vocabulary; SDK details belong behind EngineAdapter.
SDK adoption is conditional: the SDK-backed adapter is not default until it passes conformance tests.
Keep /api/harness/turn as transport and compatibility surface; runtime policy should be owned by TurnEngine and the engine boundary.
Keep compact browser UIEvents distinct from richer persisted HarnessEvents.
SDK session IDs, transcript paths, tool names, permission modes, message categories, and hook names may be retained only as explicit adapter metadata.
Product-critical reliance boundaries must be testable in Chirality terms, not only described in prompts or assumed from SDK defaults.
Keep the initial AgentEnginePort narrow; a small boundary eases stub vs SDK-backed comparison and prevents SDK-specific behavior from leaking into the product contract.

Make the conformance suite adapter-agnostic, asserting Chirality outcomes: accepted-turn persistence, stable UI events, canonical event records, terminal outcomes, permission denial, redaction, and absence of SDK-shaped leakage.
Expect some tests to be staged; SDK message categories, resume behavior, SessionStore, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and interrupt behavior depend on DEL-04-01 probe findings, so mark unsupported cases as TBD.
Preserve the stub adapter as the deterministic baseline for contract tests and fallback analysis.
Keep PRD-derived details visible but caveated; _REFERENCES.md reports a HASH_MISMATCH for docs/PRD.md requiring human confirmation.
Prefer a thin product-owned contract over a broad SDK wrapper to reduce SDK lock-in and support provider-neutral conformance.
Prefer a governed SDK subset over full SDK parity; PLAN states Chirality does not chase Claude Code feature parity but adopts SDK mechanics that accelerate the product-owned contract.
Use both type/unit tests and route/SSE compatibility checks rather than unit-only tests.
Use TBD until SDK probe results exist to prevent inaccessible or unstable SDK behavior from becoming accepted project truth.

Keep fallback criteria in runtime contract documentation and verify them through conformance where possible; K-ENGINE-5 and FR-126 make fallback a governed acceptance judgment, not just a test failure outcome.
Illustrative interface: AgentEnginePort declares runTurn(input: TurnInput): AsyncIterable<UIEvent> and optional interrupt?(sessionId: string): Promise<void>.

Conformance example: an SDK-backed adapter persists turn.accepted before invoking SDK/model execution.
Conformance example: an SDK-backed adapter maps SDK result/failure/interruption outcomes into product-owned terminal HarnessEvent records.

Conformance example: a leakage test fails if public APIs or canonical HarnessEvent fields expose SDK message names, permission modes, transcript paths, tool names, or session IDs outside explicit adapter metadata.

DEL-03-01 defines the product-owned runtime boundary for harness turn execution and the conformance suite any engine adapter must satisfy before use as the default production path.
In scope: the AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract API contract.
In scope: adapter boundary rules for stub and SDK-backed implementations.

In scope: conformance expectations for accepted-turn persistence, terminal outcomes, SSE compatibility, SDK message mapping, permission/tool boundary behavior, interrupt/cancel behavior, session resume/linkage, and redaction.
In scope: runtime contract documentation and tests associated with the contract.
Out of scope: SDK-specific message translation implementation details, except as conformance inputs and adapter-boundary expectations.
Out of scope: full TurnEngine extraction and session locking implementation, owned by DEL-03-02.
Out of scope: browser API/SSE route adapter fixtures, owned by DEL-03-03 except where conformance verifies compatibility.
Out of scope: interrupt/cancel cleanup implementation, owned by DEL-03-04 except where conformance verifies required adapter behavior.
Out of scope: SDK probe/version decision details, owned by DEL-04-01.
REQ-001: Chirality SHALL define AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract separate from SDK APIs.
REQ-002: public harness semantics SHALL remain Chirality-owned; SDK APIs, message names, transcript shape, and tool names SHALL NOT define public semantics.
REQ-003: AgentEnginePort SHALL expose runTurn(input: TurnInput): AsyncIterable<UIEvent>.
REQ-004: AgentEnginePort MAY expose interrupt?(sessionId: string): Promise<void> when the adapter can support interruption.
REQ-005: TurnInput SHALL include active session, normalized project root, persona, mode, resolved runtime options, content blocks, attachment summaries, and cancellation signal where applicable.

REQ-006: the contract SHALL cover accepted turn input, browser UIEvent yield, canonical HarnessEvent persistence, permission enforcement or invocation, permitted tool exposure, SDK session metadata linkage, interrupt/cancel behavior, and terminal outcomes.
REQ-007: SDK-specific names, IDs, permission modes, transcript paths, tool names, and hook names SHALL appear only as explicit adapter metadata.
REQ-008: the SDK-backed adapter SHALL pass the engine conformance suite before becoming the default production path.
REQ-009: a deterministic stub adapter SHALL remain available for tests.

REQ-010: engine conformance tests SHALL cover accepted-turn persistence before SDK/model execution, terminal outcome persistence, SSE compatibility, SDK message mapping, permission denial, tool exposure, interrupt/cancel behavior, session resume, and redaction.
REQ-011: the contract and tests SHALL preserve the stable browser SSE names session:init, chat:delta, chat:complete, tool:result, session:complete, turn:error, and process:exit.
REQ-012: /api/harness/turn SHALL remain a transport adapter; runtime policy belongs behind the contract and TurnEngine, not in the route.
REQ-013: the conformance suite SHALL reject provider-shaped leakage in public APIs and canonical HarnessEvent fields except as explicit adapter metadata.
REQ-014: the contract documentation SHALL record fallback criteria when SDK behavior cannot satisfy or verify a product-critical boundary.
REQ-015: requirements derived from docs/PRD.md SHALL carry the source-state warning that REF-006 is accessible but hash-mismatched in _REFERENCES.md.
